2175.subject: Zoology
2175.text: An example of stretch reflex triggered by passive muscle movement is the
2175.sol: A stretch reflex is the contraction of a muscle in response to a passive stretching of a muscle spindle within a muscle. This reflex enables the body to correct any unintended changes in body posture in a timely manner without waiting for input from the cerebral cortex as well as keeps appropriate tone in muscles. A well known example of stretch reflex is patellar reflex or knee jerk reflex, i.e., sudden kicking movement of the lower leg in response to a sharp tap on patellar tendon.

57994.text: What happens when CuSO ₄ is dissolved in water? Identify correct statements from the following
options: Anion of the salt react with water.
Its solution will turn red litmus into blue.

The CuSO ₄ will not undergo hydrolysis reaction.
57994.sol: CuSO ₄ is a salt of a weak base ( Cu(OH) ₂ ) and a strong acid ( H ₂ SO ₄ ). When dissolved in water, the Cu ²⁺ cation undergoes hydrolysis to produce H ^+ ions: Cu ²⁺ + 2 H ₂ O Cu(OH) ₂ + 2 H ^+ Due to the generation of H ^+ ions, the solution becomes acidic. Therefore, the pH of the solution will be less than 7 . The anion SO ₄²⁻ does not undergo hydrolysis as it is derived from a strong acid. An acidic solution turns blue litmus red, not red litmus blue. Answer: The pH of the solution will be less than 7 .

70962.text: Friedrich Miescher isolated nucleic acid from ________ .
70962.sol: Friedrich Miescher in 1869 isolated a new acidic substance from the nuclei of pus cells, which are primarily white blood cells. He named this substance nuclein, which was later identified as nucleic acid (DNA). Answer: white blood cells

71106.subject: Biology
71106.text: Which one of the following is a striking feature of the lobefin group of fishes that helped in evolution?
options: Coelocanth, a lobelin fish, was caught in South Africa in 1938.
They had stout and strong fins, so they could go to land and come back to water.
71106.sol: According to evolutionary history, lobefins (such as the Coelacanth) were the ancestors of the first amphibians. A striking feature of these fishes was that they possessed stout and strong fins. This anatomical adaptation allowed them to move out of water onto land and then return to water, which was a crucial step in the evolution of terrestrial vertebrates. Answer: They had stout and strong fins, so they could go to land and come back to water.

71518.subject: Biology

It is of two types: protandry, where anthers mature earlier than the stigma, and protogyny, where the stigma matures earlier than the anthers. 102258.text: Two ideal gases A and B are maintained at the same temperature and pressure. If the diameter of a molecule of gas A is twice the diameter of a molecule of gas B, what is the ratio of the mean free path of gas A to that of gas B?
102258.sol: The mean free path of a gas molecule is given by the formula: = 1 2 d^2 n where d is the molecular diameter and n is the number density of molecules. Since both gases are at the same temperature and pressure, their number density n is the same. Therefore, the mean free path is inversely proportional to the square of the molecular diameter: 1 d^2 Given that d_A = 2d_B , the ratio of their mean free paths is: _A _B = ( d_B d_A )^2 = ( d_B 2d_B )^2 = 1 4 Hence, the ratio is 1:4 . Answer: 1:4

102933.sol: The magnitude of the electric field at a point on the axial line of a short electric dipole at a distance r from its centre is given by: E_ axial = 1 4 ₀ 2p r^3 The magnitude of the electric field at a point on the equatorial line of the same short dipole at the same distance r is given by: E_ equatorial = 1 4 ₀ p r^3 Taking the ratio of the two magnitudes: E_ axial E_ equatorial = 1 4 ₀ 2p r^3 1 4 ₀ p r^3 = 2 1 Therefore, the required ratio is 2:1 . Answer: 2:1

Boiling disrupts the adsorbed layer, reducing particle charge and leading to coagulation.

121810.text: In what kind of environment are Pteridophytes commonly found?

Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions. Antheridia is a small structure that produces sperms in bryophytes or pteridophytes. In fungi the young sporangium is a white spherical structure situated at the free end of the sporangiophore. In eukaryotic cells there is an extensive compartmentalisation of cytoplasm through the presence of membrane bound organelles. Eukaryotic cells possess an organised nucleus with a nuclear envelope. In addition, eukaryotic cells have a variety of complex locomotory and cytoskeletal structures. Their genetic material is organised into chromosomes. All eukaryotic cells are not identical . Endoplasmic reticulum consists of a network of membranous tubules and helps in transport, synthesis and secret

Lysosomes are small membrane bound vesicles in the cytoplasm of cells which contain toxic enzymes. When a cell dies, these membranes rupture and the enzymes are released. 126415.sol: The propagation through vegetative multiplication is used to maintain the genetic traits of a given plant. It gives rise to genetically uniform population or clone. 126986.subject: Botany
126986.text: Joint Forest Management Concept was introduced in India during:
126986.sol: The Government of India introduced in 1980 the concept of Joint Forest Management (JFM), to work closely with the local communities for protecting and managing the forest; in return for their services to the forest, the communities get the benefit of various forest products (like fruits, medicines, rubber, gum, firewood, etc.) and thus the forest is protected sustainably.

127132.subject: Botany
127132.text: Which countries have more complete species inventories?
127132.sol: Explanation : For many taxonomic groups, species inventories are more complete in temperate than in tropical countries. Considering that an overwhelmingly large proportion of the species waiting to be discovered are in the tropics, biologists make a statistical comparison of the temperate-tropical species richness of an exhaustively studied group of insects and extrapolate this ratio to other groups of animals and plants to come up with a gross estimate of the total number of species on earth. Some extreme estimate

128089.subject: Zoology
128089.text: Read the following statements regarding the abdominal morphology of cockroaches and select the incorrect statement.
options: The female genital pouch is formed by the 7^ th , 8^ th and 9^ th sternites.
In both sexes, the 10^ th segment bears a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci.
Anal styles are short, thread-like structures that arise from the 10^ th segment in male cockroaches.
The male genital pouch is bounded dorsally by the 9^ th and 10^ th terga and ventrally by the 9^ th sternite.
128089.sol: The incorrect statement is that anal styles arise from the 10^ th segment. In male cockroaches, the short, thread-like, unjointed anal styles arise from the 9^ th sternite, not the 10^ th segment. The 10^ th segment bears the anal cerci in both males and females. The statements regarding the boundaries of the male genital pouch and the formation of the female genital pouch are anatomically correct as per NCERT. Answer: Anal styles are short, thread-like structures that arise from the 10^ th segment in male cockroac

128294.sol: FSH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females. MSH acts on the melanocytes (melanin containing cells) and regulates pigmentation of the skin . Oxytocin acts on the smooth muscles of our body and stimulates their contraction. 128647.subject: Zoology
128647.text: Which of the following match is correct?
options: ( array |c|c| Hormone & Effect Oxytocin & Milk ejection hormone array )
( array |c|c| Hormone & Effect Glucagon & Decreases blood sugar level array )
( array |c|c| Hormone & Effect Adrenaline & Decreases heart rate array )
( array |c|c| Hormone & Effect Thyroxine & Decreases BMR array )
128647.sol: Oxytocin is a hormone that causes both contraction of smooth muscle in the uterus during birth and expulsion of milk from the mammary glands during suckling. Oxytocin is produced in the neurosecretory cells of the hypothalamus but is stored and secreted by the posterior pituitary gland. Glucagon is a hormone, secreted by the ( ) (or A) cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, that increases the concentration of glucose in the blood by stimulating the metabolic breakdown of glycogen. It thus antagonizes th

128771.subject: Zoology
128771.text: What are the major proteins present in plasma?
128771.sol: Plasma is a straw coloured, viscous fluid constituting nearly 55 per cent of the blood. 90-92 per cent of plasma is water and proteins contribute 6-8 per cent of it. Fibrinogen, globulins and albumins are the major proteins .

129100.subject: Zoology
129100.text: Assertion : ADH and RAAS work in response to low blood volume and blood pressure. Reason : ANF works in response to high blood volume and blood pressure.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Ifboth assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
129100.sol: ADH (Antidiuretic hormone) and RAAS (Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System) work in response to low blood volume and low blood pressure. ADH increases the reabsorption of water in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct, and thus results in an increase in blood volume and blood pressure. RAAS is operated by JGA (Juxtaglomerular apparatus). It increases blood volume and blood pressure by two ways: Firstly, it induces the proximal convoluted tubules to reabsorb more NaCl and water and secondly, it stimulates

129187.subject: Zoology
129187.text: What is the autonomic neural system responsible for?
options: Transmitting impulses from the CNS to skeletal muscles
Transmitting impulses from the CNS to involuntary organs and smooth muscles
Transmitting impulses from tissues/organs to the CNS
Transmitting impulses from the CNS to peripheral tissues/organs
129187.sol: The CNS includes the brain and spinal cord and is the site of information processing and control.The afferent nerve fibres transmit impulses from tissues/organs to the CNS.The efferent nerve fibres transmit regulatory impulses from the CNS to the concerned peripheral tissues/organs The autonomic neural system transmits impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and smooth muscles of the body. The Visceral nervous system is the part of the peripheral nervous system that comprises the whole complex of nerves, fi

129592.subject: Zoology
129592.text: Identify the correct statements I. The outer layer of the kidney is called capsule II. Cortex is divided into outer cortex and inner medulla III. Medulla is divided into medullary pyramids IV. The cortex extends in between the medullary pyramids which is called as columns of Bertini Choose the correct option accordingly.
129592.sol: Towards the centre of the inner concave surface of the kidney is a notch called hilum through which ureter, blood vessels and nerves enter. Inner to the hilum is a broad funnel shaped space called the renal pelvis with projections called calycesThe outer layer of the kidney is a tough capsule. Inside the kidney, there are two zones, an outer cortex and an inner medulla. The medulla is divided into a few conical masses (medullary pyramids) projecting into the calyces. The cortex extends in between the medullary pyra

130070.subject: Zoology
130070.text: During extreme environmental conditions such as summer sleep (aestivation) and winter sleep (hibernation), frogs respire exclusively through their:
130070.sol: Frogs undergo aestivation (summer sleep) and hibernation (winter sleep) to protect themselves from extreme heat and cold by burrowing deep into the mud. During these dormant periods, pulmonary and buccal respiration cannot occur. The frogs rely entirely on cutaneous respiration, where gaseous exchange takes place exclusively through their moist skin. Lungs and buccal cavity are used on land, while gills are present only in the larval (tadpole) stage. Answer: skin

131176.subject: Zoology
131176.text: Mature Graafian follicle is generally present in the ovary of a healthy human female around
131176.sol: Mature Graafian follicle is generally present in the ovary of a healthy human female around 11-17 days of menstrual cycle.

131370.subject: Zoology
131370.sol: The corpus luteum plays an important role in the preparation of endometrium for the implantation of fertilized egg by secreting estrogen and progesterone hormones. But if the egg is not fertilized then the corpus luteum begins to degenerate and it stops the production of progesterone and estrogen hormones, which causes shedding of the endometrium lining with menstrual bleeding.

These repetitive DNA are separated from bulk genomic DNA as different peaks during density gradient centrifugation. The bulk DNA forms a major peak and the other small peaks are referred to as satellite DNA. 132670.subject: Zoology
132670.text: What are the three connotations of the theory of special creation according to conventional religious literature?
options: Life originated from outer space, evolution is continuous, and Earth is 4.5 billion years old
All living organisms were created as they are, diversity remains unchanged, and Earth is about 4000 years old
Life forms evolved gradually, Earth is 6,000 years old, and species are constantly changing
Life emerged from non-living matter, evolution is random, and Earth has a static history
132670.sol: Conventional religious literature tells us about the theory of special creation. This theory has three connotations. One, that all living organisms (species or types) that we see today were created as such. Two, that the diversity was always the same since creation and will be the same in future also. Three, that earth is about 4000 years old . All these ideas were strongly challenged during the nineteenth century. Based on observations made during a sea voyage in a sail ship called H.M.S. Beagle round the world, C

132919.subject: Zoology
132919.text: Which of the following pairs of structures represents homologous organs?
options: Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita
132919.sol: Homologous organs are those that share a common anatomical origin but may perform different functions, representing divergent evolution. Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita are both modifications of axillary buds. They share a common origin but perform different functions (protection and climbing, respectively), making them homologous organs. Sweet potato (a root modification) and potato (a stem modification) perform the same function of food storage but have different origins, making them analogous o

(a) Darwin’s Finches of Galapagos islands. (b) Herbicide resistant weeds. (c) Drug resistant eukaryotes. (d) Man-created breeds of domesticated animals like dogs.
132985.sol: Anthropogenic action: The evolution of various organisms due to human activities or human interference, it is called evolution due to anthropogenic action. 1. Development of antibiotics or drug resistance varieties. 2. Development of herbicides resistance varieties. 3. Artificial selection. Artificial selection: Artificial selection is the selective breeding of plants or animals for desired traits. It is done artificially by employing various breeding methods and that is why it is called artificial selection. Follo

133279.subject: Zoology
133279.sol: In our body, cell growth and differentiation is highly controlled and regulated. In cancer cells, there is breakdown of these regulatory mechanisms. Normal cells show a property called contact inhibition by virtue of which contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth. Cancer cells appears to have lost this property. As a result of this, cancerous cells just continue to divide giving rise to masses of cells called tumors

133465.subject: Zoology
133465.text: Type of Tumor Characteristic A. Benign tumor 1. Spreads to distant sites via blood B. Malignant tumor 2. Remains confined to original location C. Neoplastic cells 3. Rapidly dividing and damaging surrounding tissues D. Metastasis 4. Most feared property of malignant tumors
133465.sol: Benign tumors remain localized and do not spread. Malignant tumors are characterized by rapidly dividing cells that invade nearby tissues. Neoplastic cells in malignant tumors can spread via the bloodstream to form new tumors. Metastasis is the process by which malignant tumors spread to distant parts of the body.

133607.subject: Zoology
133607.text: Sexual stage (gametocytes) of Plasmodium occurs in
133607.sol: Inside the red blood cells, oval-shaped merozoites stop proceeding with erythrocytic cycle to increase in size and become rounded gametocytes. Male gametocytes or microgametocytes are smaller and contain a large diffused nucleus. Female gametocytes (or mega gametocytes) are larger with a small compact peripheral nucleus. These do not divide but remain as intracellular parasites within their host's blood corpuscles, until they either die or are ingested by the vectors. They give rise to gametes in insects.

134150.text: What is the most commonly used animal for transgenic research?
134150.sol: Over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice. Mice are the most commonly used animal for transgenic research due to their smaller size and easier handling. Biological products: Medicines required to treat certain human diseases can contain biological products, but such products are often expensive to make. Transgenic animals that produce useful biological products can be created by the introduction of the portion of DNA (or genes) which codes for a particular product such as human protein (α-1-antit

134551.sol: A stirred-tank reactor is usually cylindrical or with a curved base to facilitate the mixing of the reactor contents. Since DNA fragments are negatively charged molecules, they can be separated by forcing them to move towards th
The process of cutting out the separated bands of DNA from the agarose gel and extracting them from the gel pi

135316.sol: An interaction between two species wherein both species involved are benefited is called Mutualism

6a0e2776165ae1327797b37f.subject: Physics
6a0e2776165ae1327797b37f.text: Two rigid, thermally insulated tanks A and B are connected by a narrow tube fitted with a closed valve. Tank A has a volume of 5 L and contains an ideal gas at a pressure of 300 kPa and a temperature of 400 K. Tank B has a volume of 15 L and contains the same ideal gas at a pressure of 100 kPa and a temperature of 300 K. When the valve is opened and the gases are allowed to mix, what will be the final equilibrium pre
6a0e2776165ae1327797b37f.sol: Conservation of internal energy for the insulated system gives: U_A + U_B = U_f n_A C_v T_A + n_B C_v T_B = (n_A + n_B) C_v T_f n_A T_A + n_B T_B = n_f T_f From the ideal gas equation, PV = nRT , which gives nT = PV R . Substituting this into the energy equation: P_A V_A R + P_B V_B R = P_f V_f R P_A V_A + P_B V_B = P_f (V_A + V_B) Substituting the given values: 300(5) + 100(15) = P_f (5 + 15) 1500 + 1500 = 20 P_f 3000 = 20 P_f P_f = 150 kPa Answer: 150 kPa

6a0e2777165ae1327797b393.subject: Physics
6a0e2777165ae1327797b393.text: An optical system is constructed by placing three thin lenses coaxially in contact. The focal lengths of the three lenses are f , f 2 , and -f , respectively. If the lateral magnifications produced by these individual lenses are m₁ , m₂ , and m₃ , what is the equivalent power and the total lateral magnification of the system?
6a0e2777165ae1327797b393.sol: The equivalent power of a combination of thin lenses in contact is the sum of their individual powers. P = P₁ + P₂ + P₃ P = 1 f₁ + 1 f₂ + 1 f₃ Substituting the given focal lengths f₁ = f , f₂ = f 2 , and f₃ = -f : P = 1 f + 2 f - 1 f = 2 f For a system of lenses in contact, the total lateral magnification is the product of the lateral magnifications produced by the individual lenses. M = m₁ m₂ m₃ = m₁ m₂ m₃ Answer: 2 f and m₁ m₂ m₃

options: It often drives co-evolution, where the host evolves mechanisms to reject the parasite and the parasite evolve
It acts as nature's primary conduit for transferring energy fixed by autotrophs to higher trophic levels.
It may render the host more vulnerable to other ecological pressures, such as predation, by making it physical
It generally reduces the survival, growth, and reproductive fitness of the host organism, thereby decreasing i
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fb9.sol: Predation acts as nature's primary conduit for transferring energy fixed by plants (autotrophs) to higher trophic levels, not parasitism. Parasitism is an interaction where one organism (parasite) benefits at the expense of the other (host). It often drives co-evolution between the host and the parasite. Parasites typically reduce the survival, growth, and reproductive fitness of the host, thereby decreasing its population density. They can also make the host physically weak, rendering it more vulnerable to other e

Examples include biosphere reserves, national parks, and wildlife sanctuaries. Ex situ conservation refers to the conservation of components of biological diversity outside their natural habitats. Examples include zoological parks, botanical gardens, and seed banks. Therefore, zoological parks are an example of ex situ conservation, not i

95339.subject: Botany
95339.text: Which of the following is a common characteristic between earthworm, leech, and a centipede?
options: They have a ventral nerve cord
95339.sol: The ventral nerve cord possesses segmental ganglia. It is common in the earthworm, leech, and a silkworm. Earthworm and leech belong to phylum Annelida, and silkworm to phylum Arthropoda.

95493.subject: Botany
95493.text: Determine the animal that has blind sac body plan and intracellular as well as extracellular digestion.
95493.sol: Blind sac body plan and intracellular as well as extracellular digestion is seen in Cnidaria. Meandrina belongs to Phylum Cnidaria. It shows radial symmetry. Taenia (tapeworm), Psittacula (parrot) and Limulus (king crab) them show bilateral symmetry.

95904.subject: Botany
95904.sol: The Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen. Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants.

95945.subject: Botany
95945.text: The causative agent for mad cow disease is:
95945.sol: Prions: In modern medicine certain infectious neurological diseases were found to be transmitted by an agent consisting of abnormally folded protein. The agent was similar in size to viruses. These agents were called prions. The most notable diseases caused by prions are bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) commonly called mad cow disease in cattle and its analogous variant Cr–Jacob disease (CJD) in humans.

95958.subject: Botany
options: Lignin, hemicellulose, pectin and lipid cellulose
95958.sol: Cell wall consists of lignin, hemicellulose, pectin and cellulose.

96185.subject: Botany
96185.text: Tubulin protein is synthesized in which phase of cell cycle?
96185.sol: Interphase is the portion of the cell cycle that is not accompanied by observable changes under the microscope and includes the G 1 , S and G 2 phases. During interphase, the cell grows ( G 1 ) , replicates its DNA (S) and prepares for mitosis ( G 2 ) .

96576.subject: Botany
96576.text: Primary productivity does not depend upon
96576.sol: Primary production - It is the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by the plants during photosynthesis. - It is expressed in terms of weight or energy. - Primary productivity:The rate of biomass production.

96829.subject: Botany
options: Perigynous flower is found in Rose.
The keel is the characteristic feature of tulips.
The gynoecium consists of many free pistils in Michelia.
The perianth is present in the flowers of Lily.
96829.sol: Members of the Rosaceae family, like rose, peach, apple show perigynous condition. Keels are the smallest petals of Papillonaceous corolla having vexillary aestivation which is a characteristic feature of the Fabaceae family. Tulip is a member of the Liliaceae family.

97098.subject: Botany
97098.text: Twisted aestivation and axile placentation are found in:
97098.sol: China rose belongs to the Malvaceae family that has a superior ovary. The arrangement of sepals and petals is called aestivation. In twisted aestivation, the first petals overlap the next petals and so on. Along with the monadelphous condition is found in China rose in which filaments are fused to form a single bundle. Axile placentation is found in china rose in which there is a septum present and ovules are present at the center.

97149.subject: Botany
97149.text: Which of the following is a naturally occurring growth inhibitor?
97149.sol: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a growth inhibitor and are produced in plants during abscission. IAA, NAA and GA are growth promoters inducing cell division.

97267.subject: Botany
97267.text: Secondary growth brought about by vascular cambium in dicots is a type of
97267.sol: In arithmetic growth, the cell divides giving rise to two daughter cells. From which, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures to become a permanent cell. This kind of growth rate is shown by meristematic cells. Plasticity is ability of the tissues to form different structures in response to environmental conditions. Senescence is the deterioration phase with respect to ageing of a cell or tissue or an organism.

97276.subject: Botany
97276.text: The hormone that induces apical dominance and the hormone that acts as an antagonist to this process is
97276.sol: In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits growth of the lateral buds, a phenomenon called apical dominance and is induced by auxins like NAA, 2,4 D, IAA etc. Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) or addition of cytokinins like zeatin, kinetic etc., usually results in the growth of lateral buds. It is widely applied in tea plantation, hedge making. Cytokinin helps to overcome apical dominance.

305671.text: Forming three sides of a square, a steel frame ( K = 45 W m ⁻¹ ^ C⁻¹ ) has a total length of 60 cm and a cross sectional area of 0.20 cm ^2 . The two free ends are maintained at 20^ C and 40^ C . Determine the rate of heat flow through a cross section of the frame.

306243.subject: Physics
306243.text: By ⁺ -emission, ⁵⁷ Co decays into ⁵⁷ Fe . The produced ⁵⁷ Fe is initially in an excited state and transitions to the ground state by emitting -rays. The half-life for the ⁺ -decay is 270 days , while the half-life for the -emission is 10⁻⁸ s . If a ⁵⁷ Co sample currently emits 5.0 10⁹ gamma rays per second, what time will elapse until the gamma ray emission rate drops to 2.5 10⁹ per second?
306243.sol: The decay sequence is ⁵⁷ Co ^+ ⁵⁷ Fe ^ * ⁵⁷ Fe . Since the half-life of ⁵⁷ Co ( 270 days ) is much greater than the half-life of the excited ⁵⁷ Fe ^ * state ( 10⁻⁸ s ), secular equilibrium is established almost instantaneously. In secular equilibrium, the rate of formation of the daughter nucleus is equal to its rate of decay. Thus, the activity of ⁵⁷ Fe ^ * ( -emission rate) is equal to the activity of ⁵⁷ Co ( ⁺ -emission rate). The -emission rate will therefore decay with the half-life of the parent ⁵⁷ Co nucleus

306783.subject: Physics
306783.text: Select the correct statements from the following.
options: All atoms possess a magnetic moment.
All protons possess a magnetic moment.
All nuclei possess a magnetic moment.
All electrons possess a magnetic moment.
306783.sol: Statement (1) is incorrect. Atoms with paired electrons and zero nuclear spin (e.g., ⁴₂ He , ¹²₆ C ) have a net magnetic moment of zero. Statement (2) is correct. A proton is a spin- 1/2 particle and possesses an intrinsic magnetic moment. Statement (3) is incorrect. Nuclei with an even number of protons and an even number of neutrons (even-even nuclei) have zero nuclear spin and zero magnetic moment. Statement (4) is correct. An electron is a spin- 1/2 particle and possesses an intrinsic magnetic moment.
